title: Boomerang order cadence and SKU handoff notes
content:
Purpose:
Quick working notes for the 'boomerang' ordering cadence experiment and SKU handoff that lets us reduce immediate cash outlay by recycling short-leased/returned boards between regions while new long-lead SKUs arrive. This is an ops-heavy pilot to smooth 6–12 week lead time cliffs.

One-line summary:
We plan 3 concurrent lanes: (1) Reserved shipments for long-lead HQ orders (A100/RTX9000 class), (2) Boomerang pool of short leases and tested returns (T4/RTX6000) to bridge regional gaps, (3) Opportunistic spot purchase buffer for burst capacity. Goal: keep regional RTT < 2s tail and 10% headroom for 99th pct usage.

Current inventory snapshot (as of 2025-02-10):
SKU | target | on-hand | allocated | runweeks@currentburn | notes
A100-80GB | 420 | 312 | 280 | 10w | ordered 2025-01-15, ETA 2025-04-20
H100-80GB | 180 | 92 | 82 | 6w | partial arrivals, quality checks ongoing
RTX9000-64GB | 60 | 22 | 20 | 4w | reserved for private customers (east-us)
RTX6000-48GB | 240 | 160 | 145 | 12w | primary boomerang pool candidate
T4-16GB | 500 | 430 | 390 | 8w | good for embedding workload bursts

Regional runway matrix (weeks of runway at nominal burn):
- US-West: 9w (high traffic, can borrow 20 RTX6000 from boomerang pool)
- US-East: 7w (some reserved capacity for enterprise on RTX9000)
- EU-Central: 11w (slower growth this quarter)
- APAC-SG: 6w (fast growth; consider priority for next leased batch)

Lead time assumptions (updated vendor intel, Feb 2025):
- A100 family: 12–16 weeks from PO; high variability +/- 3w
- H100 family: 8–12 weeks; possible partial shipments
- RTX9000 family: 10–14 weeks, custom rack mounts add 2w
- RTX6000 equivalent (channel buys / refurbished): 2–6 weeks (best for boomerang)

Boomerang pool design notes:
- Definition: boards that can be returned, sanity-checked, reimaged, and redeployed in a different region within 7–14 days of return.
- Eligibility: must pass burn-in (48h), KV cache test, and thermals; prefer non-binned retail or refurbished vendor lot with traceability.
- Telemetry tagging: every boomerang board gets a 'boomerang-id' and quick health metadata stored in fleetdb for 90 days.
- Movement policy: borrow-lend TTL 30 days, cross-region transfer only if regional runway < 6w and transfer won't breach donor region target runway.

Ordering cadence proposals (3 options):
1) Staggered bulk (baseline): large POs every quarter for long-lead SKUs; boomerang as emergency only. Pros: fewer POs, lower price. Cons: cliff risk.
2) Rolling tranches (preferred): place smaller tranche orders every 4–6 weeks for A100/H100 to smooth arrivals; maintain boomerang pool sized to 20% of peak regional deficit. Pros: smoother capacity, easier QA. Cons: slightly higher unit prices/fees.
3) Lease-first hybrid: lease short-term cards for 8–12 weeks to bridge while waiting for long-lead arrivals; convert to purchases on favorable market. Pros: cash flexibility. Cons: complexity in logistics and security (data sanitization).

Decision matrix (quick):
- If expected lead time delta > 8 weeks and regional runway <= 6w -> roll tranches + boomerang transfer.
- If vendor confirms partial shipments possible -> accept smaller deliveries and reserve staging racks at West HUB.
- For APAC priority customers -> allocate from boomerang first, mixed with leased burst.

Operational checklists (short):
- Procurement: confirm tranche PO release schedule; include partial-shipment option and early-ship clause. Owner: Jun Park.
- SRE/Logistics: prepare 2 staging racks per region for incoming partials; pre-wire 10% of racks for quick swap. Owner: Leah O'Connor.
- Test & QA: define 48h burn-in recipe, thermal throttling thresholds, firmware flash image id, KV-cache flush script. Owner: Marco Liu.
- Security/Compliance: ensure returned boards are wiped and attested; log KMS keys rotated when hardware crosses customer tenancy. Owner: Security Team contact: security-team@redwood.ai

Cost & runway calculus (back-of-envelope):
- Lease lane: $/week per T4 ~ $350, RTX6000 ~ $1,900, A100 lease not usually available cheaply. For bridging a 10-card regional deficit for 8 weeks on RTX6000 lease: 10 * 1,900 * 8 = $152k (compare to buy delta vs used/resell price).
- Rolling tranche premium estimated at +6% unit cost vs single PO; expected to reduce cliff-induced emergency leasing by ~70%.

Risk log (open):
- Vendor churn or factory slowdowns may push A100 beyond 20 weeks (contingency: prioritize H100 where compatible).
- Cross-region shipping customs delays (APAC can see 2–4w hold). We need HS codes and pre-clear docs.
- Boomerang health skew: reused boards exhibit slightly higher failure rates (observed +0.8% after 6 months). Plan: cap boomerang use to non-SLA-critical lanes.

Open questions / discussion points for 2025-03-03 ops sync:
- How big should the boomerang pool be to support APAC growth if APAC demand doubles in Q3? (initial ask: scale to 30% of APAC 12w deficit)
- Can finance approve rolling tranche pricing with 6% premium vs cash-flow benefit? Need CFO sign-off on tranche pilot.
- Are vendors willing to commit to partial-shipment SLAs and penalty clauses? Procurement to follow up with top-3 vendors by 2025-02-20.

Action items (owner + ETA):
- Jun: draft tranche PO template with partial-shipment clause and penalty language (ETA 2025-02-18).
- Leah: setup staging rack wire diagram and inventory tags for quick-swap (ETA 2025-02-25).
- Marco: publish 48h burn-in automation on infra repo and PR for test thresholds (ETA 2025-02-22).
- Asha: coordinate finance sync and compile cost-benefit slides for exec by 2025-02-28.

Appendix A — quick sample schedule (weeks):
- Week 0 (today): commit tranche schedule + align vendors.
- Week 2: lease 40 RTX6000 units for APAC bridge (if approved).
- Week 6: expect first tranche A100 partial arrival (20%).
- Week 10: second tranche A100 arrival, reduce boomerang usage by 50%.

Notes to self / raw observations (informal):
- spoke with vendor rep (Carlos) — plausible to get 10% earlier shipment if we accept a premium and supply a local customs broker.
- Slack thread: #procurement has initial vendor quotes; share in meeting.
- Performance note: boomerang boards show slightly slower sustained throughput under 1ms tail in stress tests; acceptable for internal-only routing.

Bottom line: roll-tranche pilot + boomerang pool seems the least risky path to avoid a hard cliff. Need procurement + finance sign-off and a small lease cushion for APAC.
plain_text_preview: Working sheet: boomerang ordering cadence and handoff. Key owners: Jun, Leah, Marco. Decision: roll-tranches + boomerang pool recommended. Open Qs: finance sign-off and vendor partial-shipment SLAs.
